newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Paranapanema has no news of Yauliyacu.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Paranapanema has no news of Yauliyacu.

text.p: Brazil's Paranapanema has not officially been informed that it has lost its option to purchase Peruvian polymetallic unit Empresa Minera Yauliyacu, said a company director.
But if this proves to be the case, the company will take legal action over the decision, said Antonio Miguel.
"We have received no formal reply...But if this is the case, we will go to the courts in Peru because we understand that we have fulfilled all requirements," Miguel said.
Earlier today in Peru, a spokesman for Peruvian state miner Centromin said the Brazilian company had lost its option because it did not provide paperwork and the necessary guarantee.
The spokesman also said that the mine would now be awarded to local company Minera Casapalca S.A..
Paranapanema won the auction for Yauliyacu for $12.7 million last December. It also offered to invest $100 million over a five year period.

According to Miguel, a Peruvian bank sent a letter to Centromin on February 24, the deadline for necessary documents to be submitted, saying that it had received the funds and a stand-by bank guarantee from Banco do Brasil.
In the letter, the Peruvian bank said that it was in the process of checking the documents so that it could issue its formal guarantee.
"We have made all efforts and fulfilled all conditions and we will take legal action for what we think are our rights," Miguel said.
The Paranapanema group which was formed last year includes copper producer Caraiba Metais, zinc unit Companhia Paraibuna de Metais and tin producer Mamore (formerly known as Paranapanema).

According to Centromin, the Yauliyacu reserve has proven and probable reserves of silver, zinc, lead and copper totalling 7.3 million tonnes while the unit's potential reserves total 14.7 million tonnes.
In 1995, 746,000 tonnes of mineral were extracted from the site.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
